Syscall and ioctl entry points, command dispatch and privilege checks.

findings.text: ELF note headers exist in two widths with parallel meaning: each carries a name length plus a descriptor length plus a type tag, exposed under distinct width-specific type names.

Core-dump style note identifiers are partitioned by architecture with a shared LINUX owner label: ARM SME and floating point and protection and guard state near 0x40c through 0x410, ARCv2 near 0x600, device dump near 0x700, MIPS DSP and FP mode and SIMD near 0x800 through 0x802, RISC-V CSR and vector and tagged address and shadow stack near 0x900 through 0x903, LoongArch config and CSR and vector extensions and translation and hardware debug near 0xa00 through 0xa06.

Version definition records in both widths carry version and flags and index and entry count and hash plus offsets for auxiliary data and chaining; auxiliary records carry a name offset plus a chain offset.
AArch64 GNU property ABI defines one feature-word selector value and one branch-protection feature bit occupying the least significant bit of that word.

Extended socket error reports carry an errno plus origin plus type plus code plus pad plus auxiliary info, followed by a variant payload that is either a plain 32 bit datum or a small RFC4884 record with length and flags and reserved byte; the offender address is specified to begin immediately after the header.

Error-queue origins number none as zero through local, ICMP, ICMPv6, transmit status, zero-copy and transmit-time as one through six, with timestamping aliased to transmit status; defined codes mark zero-copy copied and transmit-time invalid parameter and missed deadline, and one flag marks invalid RFC4884 data.

Software timestamp reports carry exactly three timestamps; the legacy form selects kernel old versus userspace timestamp type by build context while the 64-bit form always uses fixed-width kernel timestamps, and the documented stage order is driver handoff then scheduler entry then acknowledgement then completion.

Legacy link-settings record carries a command tag plus capability masks plus a split link-speed representation plus duplex and port and PHY address and transceiver and autonegotiation and MDIO support fields plus packet maxima plus high speed half plus media-dependent-interface controls plus peer advertisement plus reserved words.
Two small helpers convert between a full 32-bit link speed and its two 16-bit halves stored in the legacy settings record, one splitting on store and one rejoining on load.

Driver information carries a command tag plus fixed-length driver and version and firmware and bus and ROM strings plus reserved bytes plus counts for private flags and statistics and test and dump lengths; wake-on-LAN carries command plus capability and option masks plus a short password; generic value and tunable records carry command plus data or identifier plus type plus length plus trailing payload.

Management constants fix firmware and bus and ROM string lengths at 32, MDIO clause support as bit values, storm-prevention auto and disable markers, downshift default and disable markers, fast-link-down on and off markers, and EDPD default-timing and no-transmit and disable markers.

Device and PHY tunable selectors are enumerations beginning with an unspecified value and ending with a count sentinel, with typed width variants for the generic tunable path and named feature selectors for the PHY path.

Register and EEPROM access records each carry command plus version or magic plus offset or length plus trailing bytes; energy-efficient-ethernet state carries command plus supported and advertised and peer masks plus active and enabled flags plus transmit low-power settings plus reserved words; module info carries command plus type plus EEPROM length plus reserved words.

Coalescing parameters carry interrupt-pacing intervals and frame maxima for receive and transmit in normal, IRQ, low-rate and high-rate bands plus adaptive enables plus rate thresholds and sampling interval; ring sizing carries maxima and current depths for receive classes and transmit; channel sizing carries maxima and current counts for receive, transmit, other and combined; pause parameters carry command plus autonegotiation plus receive and transmit enables.

Extended link-down reporting uses one top-level reason selector covering negotiation, training, logical mismatch, signal integrity, cabling, EEPROM, calibration, power budget, overheat, module, speed policy and controller request, with a separate detailed sub-enumeration per reason whose values start at one.

String-set selectors enumerate families for tests, statistics, private flags, filters, features, hash functions, tunables, PHY statistics, link modes, message classes, wake modes, timestamping roles, tunnel types and grouped standard and media-access and control and RMON and PHY counters, ending in a count sentinel, with fixed 32-character string length and aggregate versus embedded versus physical MAC source selectors.
Module power policy and mode use small one-based selectors distinguishing high versus automatic policy and low versus high operating mode.

Power-sourcing equipment uses a bitmask for unknown versus single-pair versus clause-33 types, plus one-based administrative selectors for disabled versus enabled and multi-stage delivery selectors covering unknown, disabled, searching, delivering and fault-like outcomes with technology-specific terminal states.

Clause-33 extended power states enumerate error, maintenance-power-signature validity, enable, detection, voltage-limit, overload, data-link power type, power availability and short conditions, each refined by a one-based sub-enumeration describing the specific port, wiring, budget, voltage, thermal, host-crash or protocol cause.

MAC merge verification progresses from unknown through initial and verifying to succeeded or failed or disabled, while module firmware flashing progresses from started through in-progress to completed or error.

String, string-set-size, self-test, statistics and permanent-address records all carry a command tag plus set or flag or count fields plus a trailing flexible payload sized by an explicit length, mask or count field.

Test flags use low-order bits for offline, failed and external loopback control and completion; device feature flags use widely spaced bits for transmit and receive VLAN, large-receive, N-tuple filtering and receive hashing; one flow constant marks IPv4 network-filter input.

Receive-flow steering describes IPv4 and IPv6 match fields for TCP/UDP/SCTP ports, IPsec identifiers, and generic four-byte payload plus traffic class and protocol bytes; a union selects one header interpretation or raw bytes, an extension record adds destination address plus VLAN tags plus opaque data, and the top rule joins flow type plus value and mask unions plus extension value and mask plus queue cookie plus location.

Every management record in this group begins with a command discriminator, fixed text fields use compile-time lengths, and variable payloads are carried in trailing flexible arrays whose extent is governed by a companion length, count or mask field rather than by the base type size.

Callers must validate trailing lengths before copying register, EEPROM, string, test, statistics, address and tunable payloads; must not dereference the offender trailer beyond the supplied control message; must preserve both halves of split link speed; and must account for the build-dependent timestamp width in the legacy timestamp record.
